title: Getting started with compfit
text: basic workflow three calls: load, fit, plot. rest guide covers step.
code: library(compfit)  # A scenario is a folder of three sheets: model, data, and optional dummy series. sc <- load_scenario("path/to/MyScenario",                     combined_file = "dataCombined.csv",                     dummy_file    = "dataDummy.csv",                     params_file   = "modelParams.csv")  # Fit by maximum likelihood. backend = "r" runs entirely in R, with no Julia. fit <- fitCompartmentalModel(sc$modelParams, sc$dataCombined,                              method = "lbfgsb",                              solver = solver_control(backend = "r")) summary(fit)  # Inspect the fit (and any dummy series) as a grid of per-stream panels. plot_fit(fit, data_dummy = sc$dataDummy)$grid

title: Getting started with compfit
text: Solving ODE, Bayesian fits drawing posterior, can run three backends. Pick one solver_control(backend = ...): Maximum-likelihood fits give answer every backend, just faster Julia. Bayesian fits differences matter: "julia" main path: fast NUTS, every family every data-cell type. "r" uses gradient-free sampler (BayesianTools DEzs), seeded quick MLE fit. much slower mixes far worse, best small model sanity check. real inference use Julia Stan. "stan" gives gradient-based NUTS Julia. three backends now score every data-cell type (observed, censored, interval [,B]/[,B]~s, asymmetric) four families. censored count data Stan actually strongest option (see CDF note ). Every data-cell type now works three Bayesian backends. one remaining backend nuance Julia score censored/interval/asymmetric cell discrete family (see CDF note); Stan R can. Everything downstream (posterior_report(), plot_prior_posterior(), ) works whichever backend pick. Julia backend needs one-time setup per session. first call also installs required Julia packages (OrdinaryDiffEq, Turing, Distributions), takes minutes; later calls quick: bridge also initialises lazily, setup_julia() mainly just slow part front. R Stan backends need Julia .

title: Getting started with compfit
text: Pass method = "bayes" bayes_control() spec, choose sampler solver backend ("julia", "stan", "r"). bayes_control(progress = FALSE) silences sampler’s progress output backend. Inspect posterior convergence: useful check compare posterior MLE fit model:
code: fit_b <- fitCompartmentalModel(   modelParams  = sc$modelParams,   dataCombined = sc$dataCombined,   method       = "bayes",   solver       = solver_control(),                        # or backend = "stan" / "r"   bayes        = bayes_control(chains = 4, iter = 2000, warmup = 1000) ) posterior_report(fit_b)        # convergence verdict plus means and intervals posterior_means(fit_b) posterior_intervals(fit_b, p = 0.95) plot_prior_posterior(fit_b)    # prior vs posterior, per parameter identifiability_report(fit_b)  # narrowing, coverage, correlation diagnostics fit_mle <- fitCompartmentalModel(sc$modelParams, sc$dataCombined, "lbfgsb") compare_to_mle(fit_b, fit_mle) # posterior mean and median vs MLE

title: Optimiser settings — optim_control
text: Bundle optimiser settings maximum-likelihood methods. Two optimisers share control: deterministic quasi-Newton **L-BFGS-B** (`method = "lbfgsb"`, gradient finite differences) stochastic **DEoptim** differential-evolution search (`method = "deoptim"`, global method robust multi-modal / rugged objectives slower). `maxit`/`factr` options apply L-BFGS-B; `itermax`/`NP_mult`/`CR`/`F`/ `trace`/`seed` apply DEoptim; `progress` applies . Settings optimiser simply ignored, one control object works MLE method.

title: Optimiser settings — optim_control
code: optim_control(   opt_method = "L-BFGS-B",   maxit = 1000,   factr = 1e+07,   itermax = 1000,   NP_mult = 10,   CR = 0.9,   F = 0.8,   trace = 50,   seed = NULL,   progress = TRUE )

title: Optimiser settings — optim_control
text: opt_method `optim()` method used `lbfgsb` path. Normally `"L-BFGS-B"` (box-constrained); `"Brent"` 1-D alternative. search runs normalised \[0,1\] box, method must support box bounds. maxit L-BFGS-B: maximum iterations stops (default 1000). factr L-BFGS-B: convergence tolerance multiple machine epsilon; smaller = stricter/slower (default 1e7, .e. ~1e-8 relative). itermax DEoptim: maximum number generations (default 1000). NP_mult DEoptim: population size multiple number fitted quantities (`NP = NP_mult * d`). DEoptim authors recommend >= 10 (default); lower faster explores less. CR DEoptim: crossover probability \[0,1\] (default 0.9). F DEoptim: differential weighting (mutation) factor, typically \[0,2\] (default 0.8). trace DEoptim: print best value every `trace` generations (default 50). Ignored `progress = FALSE`. seed Optional RNG seed stochastic `deoptim` method, reproducible fits. `lbfgsb`/`hypercube` already deterministic ignore – except `|random` parameter start (see modelParams grammar `vignette("compfit")`) draws L-BFGS-B start seed, setting makes random warm start reproducible . progress Show optimisation progress. `TRUE` (default) prints running best objective time loss improves (DEoptim) per-generation `trace`. `FALSE` silences quiet fit – best solution still tracked recovered. (Bayesian sampler's progress controlled separately, [bayes_control()]'s `progress`.)

Unrecognised strings fall back `"lsoda"`. **Stan**: `"rk45"` (default, non-stiff), `"bdf"` (stiff),     `"adams"` (non-stiff multistep).
